articles.headline: Sacred to the Memory of Mrs. M. C. Weaver (poem)
articles.summary: Memorial verses: "Thou art gone home. From all the cares / Of life, thy happy soul is free." Dated Norfolk, Va., March 22d, 1864; signature illegible on the film. On the same page, "Lines on the Death of Mrs. Weaver," signed A. C. W., Providence, March 26th, 1864.

articles.headline: Baltimore Correspondence
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I know that you, with all the black patriots of the country, will be pleased to learn that Maryland, the most important Border State in the Union, is in motion. Dated Baltimore, Md., March 19, 1864. Reports the Bethel (Saratoga Street) mass meetings for enlistment addressed by Senator Henry Wilson, with Rev. A. W. Wayman as pastor and Colonel Bowman recruiting.

articles.headline: A Humane Appeal (Recorder for colored soldiers)
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: An appeal to the citizens of Philadelphia and elsewhere on behalf of our brave colored soldiers of the United States, who have left their homes, their wives, their children ... many have written to the editor of this paper to know why it is that they cannot be supplied with our paper. Donations to Box 2076 [box number blurred], Philadelphia, or to 619 Pine St.

articles.headline: To Our Kind Friends and Patrons (Old Folks' Continental Concert for the soldiers' paper fund)
articles.author: A. Burris
articles.summary: I have seen the very humane appeal made by the Editor of the Christian Recorder for aid to send the Christian Recorder to our brave colored soldiers now upon the battle-field ... we therefore agree to give one of our interesting, amusing and entertaining Old Folks' Continental Concerts, on Thursday evening, April 21st, at the Sansom St. Hall, half of the proceeds to go towards sending the paper to our brave troops. Signed A. Burris and Troupe, Phila., March 12th, 1864. A separate editorial notice ('Concert') repeats the date and urges a full house.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Charles Brisco)
articles.author: Elizabeth Brisco
articles.summary: Information is wanted of Charles Brisco, who left Virginia, some four or five years ago, to wait upon Lieutenant Fairfax, on a steamer for San Francisco ... Any information concerning him may be left at the Book and Christian Recorder office, No. 619 Pine Street, Philadelphia. Signed (F.?) Elizabeth Brisco, his wife. N.B. His mother and sister in Georgetown, D.C.: Cynthia Brisco and Mrs. Mary A. Dove. Dated Mar 20.

articles.headline: To Agents of Our Paper / To Our Unpaying Subscribers (General Conference to meet in Philadelphia, May 1)
articles.summary: We once more call upon you ... to remit forthwith the amount due us. We are to settle up at the General Conference. Our four years' service ends at the General Conference. We must have all returns made by the 10th and 20th of April. The second notice adds that the General Conference ... will meet in Philadelphia on the first day of May.

articles.headline: Colored Troops of the United States (editorial on equal pay and protection)
articles.summary: The recruiting of colored men for the war has slacked off considerably within the last few weeks, and there is some cause for that. 1st. Before Congress met, the colored men were assured by men who were recruiting by the authority of the government, that they would get the same pay and every privilege that white soldiers received ... 2d. The government has not, as yet, given the colored people (if taken by the rebels) assurance of their ever being exchanged.

articles.headline: The African Methodist Episcopal Church and the Methodist Episcopal Church and the Coming General Conferences
articles.summary: It is evident that God has done, and is doing, and intends to do a great work for those of his people who have been so long oppressed. Proposes that the two General Conferences, both meeting in Philadelphia, send delegates to agree on the A.M.E. Church's mission among the freedpeople of the South.

articles.headline: Letter on the Olustee battle (54th Massachusetts)
articles.author: E. D. W.
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: It is with much pleasure that I avail myself to inform you concerning our last battle ... The battle took place in a grove called Olustee. Describes the 8th U.S. (first colored regiment in the battle), the 54th Mass. and the 1st N.C.; protests unequal pay. Signed E. D. W., Co. B, 54th Mass. Vol., Jacksonville, Fla., March 18th, 1864. Out of town; noted for the Olustee aftermath.

articles.headline: Letter of condolence to Rev. Elisha Weaver (Portsmouth, Va.)
articles.author: H. M. Turner
articles.summary: Rev. Elisha Weaver: Having had a Recorder sent me by a lady friend of Washington city ... and having there, to my great surprise, seen recorded the death of that estimable lady, known as the Rev. Mrs. Weaver, I felt it to be a duty indispensably due my brother in the gospel to testify my sympathy in your irreparable bereavement. Signed H. M. Turner, Chaplain of 1st U.S. Col'd Troops, Portsmouth, Va., March 24th, 1864.
people: deceased; wife of Rev. Elisha Weaver

articles.headline: Eulogy on the Death of Mrs. Mary C. Weaver, the Late Consort of the Rev. Elisha Weaver
articles.author: J. H. Turpin
articles.summary: We lament the loss of our citizen, and sister Sabbath School teacher, and devoted friend, when we review that capacious and uncommon power of memory, which the God of nature had given her ... Farewell, Sister Mary, until the general resurrection morning ... I expect to hail you, my dear mother, upon the plains of eternal felicity. Signed J. H. Turpin, Western Theological Seminary, March 25th, 1864.
people: deceased (Mrs.); Sabbath School teacher; wife of Rev. Elisha Weaver

articles.headline: Wilberforce University receipts (Philadelphia Conference entry)
articles.author: J. A. Shorter
articles.summary: Cincinnati, March 28th, 1864. Mr. Editor: Please allow me again to call the attention of the public ... to the following receipts in behalf of Wilberforce University. Under Philadelphia Conference: through their Treasurer, M. Hall, 106.00, and also 115.00, bad 2.00, 111.00; total 217.00. Continued on p. 3 with a note that moneys received by Bishop Payne in Baltimore, Philadelphia and other places are not included.

articles.headline: Letter from Bordentown (revival; Wilberforce collection)
articles.author: T. A. Cuff [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I thought it would be interesting to numerous readers of your valuable paper, to hear a word from this part of the Lord's vineyard ... We have been holding a protracted meeting for the last seven or eight weeks ... Twenty-five have professed a saving faith in Christ Jesus the Lord, and have added to the church, thirty-six. I laid the claims of the Wilberforce before my people on last Sabbath, the 27th inst., and received the sum of twelve dollars and thirty-nine cents. Bordentown, March 28th, 1864.

articles.headline: Obituary (Eliza Burr, Attleborough)
articles.author: O. Conover
articles.summary: Departed this life after ten days or two weeks' sickness, on the morning of March 21st, 1864, Sister Eliza Burr, wife of George Burr, in the seventy-first year of her age ... Sister Eliza was a member of the A. M. E. Church from her early days, and I might say from the rise of the A. M. E. Church in Attleborough. Signed O. Conover, Attleborough, March 26th [day blurred], 1864.

articles.headline: African Civilization Society: circular, constitution and officers
articles.author: Henry M. Wilson
articles.summary: Office of the African Civilization Society, New York City. The accumulating interests which are clustering around our race, amid the revolutions in this country, have prompted the African Civilization Society to enter more energetically on the discharge of the duties contemplated in its organization. Officers: President Rev. Geo. W. Le Vere (Brooklyn); Vice-Presidents include Bishop D. A. Payne, Rev. Willis Nazrey, Bishop, A. M. E. Church, Philadelphia, Benj. Coates, Esq., Philadelphia, and Rev. articles.headline: Lines on the Death of Mary C. Weaver (poem)
articles.summary: Ah! yes, she is dead; the last struggle is o'er, / Her friends and her kindred shall see her no more ... For Mary is happy, dear Mary is blessed. Signed Susan Paul Vashon, Pittsburg, Pa., March 27th, 1864 (out-of-town author).

articles.headline: An Unfounded Report (Bishop Nazrey and the Baltimore Conference)
articles.author: J. P. B. Eddy
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: It is reported that Bishop Nazrey wrote to a member of the Baltimore Conference, to know what they wanted him to do, or what they wanted of him; which report is not true. I have seen the Bishop on the subject, and he informed me that it was not so. March 30, 1864.

articles.headline: Meeting of Annual Conferences; arrangements for General Conference delegates
articles.summary: The Ohio and Baltimore Annual Conferences meet before the sitting of the General Conference ... The Baltimore Conference meets in Washington City on the 14th inst. Bishop Payne will preside. The Ohio Conference will meet in Pittsburg, Pa., on the 16th inst. Bishop Quinn will preside. And, immediately on the adjournment of these Conferences, the delegates will repair to the General Conference. The Rev. William D. W. Schureman and the other brethren are making preparations for the reception of the brethren. Same page: Weaver's notice that delegates west of the mountains will pay full fare Pittsburg to Philadelphia on the Pennsylvania Central and return free; Dr. Revels's arrangement for Missouri and Indiana delegates.

articles.headline: Letter from Port Republic, N.J. (new church; members gone to war)
articles.author: Harriet A. Smith [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: We have had so far to go to worship that we concluded to build a church nearer. We commenced it in June, and it was finished by the last of October. It was dedicated to the service of God, by Elder R. Barney, assisted by Elder J. P. Campbell. After our little church was finished, we received eight members, and five on probation ... on the 3d of January, five of our dear brethren bade us farewell, to go to fight in defence of our country. Port Republic, N.J., March 28th [?], 1864.

articles.headline: On the Death of Mrs. Mary C. Weaver (poem)
articles.author: Jane E. Thompson
articles.summary: Oh! weep not for Mary, she has gone to her rest; / To the land of the faithful, the home of the blest ... Which beamed with delight when her husband was nigh. Signed Jane E. Thompson (no place given).
people: deceased (Mrs.); wife of Rev. Elisha Weaver

articles.headline: From Jacksonville, Florida: the 8th USCT at Olustee
articles.author: Rufus S. Jones
articles.summary: Jacksonville, Florida, March 20th, 1864. Expedition to Florida. In my last letter I stated that the Federal forces were on their way to Lake City ... The Eighth, which had been left at Ten-mile Station, formed a line of march on the 15th of February, for Baldwin. The battle of Olustee, or Ocean Pond, on the 20th of February, will be long remembered by the Eighth. Colonel Charles W. Fribley of the Eighth fell, mortally wounded; Major Loren Burritt took command and fell badly wounded; Captain R. C. Bailey of Company B took command; praises Dr. Alex. P. Heichhold [VERIFY], surgeon, for collecting the colored wounded. Signed Rufus S. Jones, Sergeant-Major Eighth U.S.C.T.

articles.headline: Presentation to President Lincoln (Mrs. Caroline Johnson's wax fruit)
articles.summary: The Washington correspondent of the Newark Advertiser writes as follows: An affair of considerable interest came off at the White House, on Saturday last, in the presence of a small party of visitors, being the formal presentation of a very choice collection of wax fruits to 'Abraham and Mary Lincoln,' from Mrs. Caroline Johnston [as printed; later 'Mrs. Johnson'], a highly respectable colored friend, of Philadelphia, as a testimonial of her appreciation of the President's services in behalf of her oppressed race ... the presentation speech was made by the Rev. James Hamilton, a Baptist clergyman of the above city. The work is valued at $3?0. Editorial addition: Rev. James Hamilton has been in our city nearly two years; he is pastor of a Baptist Church; President Lincoln and his lady received him and Mrs. Johnson very kindly.

articles.headline: Congress and the Pay of Colored Troops (editorial)
articles.summary: We are continually getting letters from our noble and brave colored soldiers, who have risked their lives for the sake of the Union ... They have been offered seven dollars per month, but have refused to take that sum ... we call upon Congress to at once pass a law, that these men shall at once be paid the same as all other soldiers are paid. Same page: notes on the North-Western Christian Advocate and A.M.E./M.E. union, revivals, Rev. Page Tyler wins the premium, the Christian Commission (George H. Stuart), and a reminder that the General Conference sits in Philadelphia the first Monday in May.

articles.headline: Letter from the 3rd USCT near Jacksonville (Olustee; Supervisory Committee package)
articles.author: George Heimach
articles.summary: Camp of 3d Reg't U.S.C.T., near Jacksonville, Fla., April 1st, 1864. Dear Sir: Your letter to Lieut. Baker, dated Feb. ... has, after a long journey, at last come safely to hand ... Allow me, sir, to thank you kindly, as also Mr. Webster [VERIFY], chairman of the Supervisory Committee, for forwarding the same. Describes the landing at Jacksonville, Baldwin, Barber's Ford and the battle of Olustee, praising the 8th USCT, 54th Mass. and 1st N.C. (colored), and the 3d USCT under Colonel Tilghman at Baldwin. Signed George Heimach, Second Lieut. Co. G, Third U.S.C.T. (officer of a Camp William Penn regiment; not linked).

articles.headline: An Important Letter from a Teacher of the Freedmen (Norfolk)
articles.author: Sallie
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: The promise I made you when in Philadelphia, to correspond with the Recorder, has hitherto remained unfulfilled ... A few weeks ago there was but one colored female teacher in this city; now there are four. Reports the March 30 celebration of Virginia's abolition with speeches by Revs. S. B. Peck [?], T. Henson, W. Yeocum [?] and J. M. Brown. Signed Sallie, Norfolk, Virginia, April 14th, 1864.

articles.headline: Editorial Correspondence: The Baltimore Annual Conference
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: This Conference met on the 14th inst., in Union Church, Washington, D.C., Bishop Payne presiding ... The Rev. Benjamin T. Tanner was elected Secretary. We left Philadelphia on last Sunday night, the 17th inst., in company with the Revs. J. P. Campbell and John Wright, for the City of Washington, and arrived in that city by six o'clock next morning, and stopped with our old friends, Mr. and Mrs. Wright. Reports on John M. Brown's Norfolk mission, J. D. S. Hall, Henry M. Turner (marked by smallpox); Weaver left Wednesday morning for the Pittsburg (Ohio) Conference.
people: travelled with the editor from Philadelphia to the Baltimore Conference (Rev.)

articles.headline: Letter from Camp near Annapolis: the 43d USCT leaves Camp William Penn
articles.author: John C. Brock
articles.summary: Camp near Annapolis, April 21st, 1864. Dear Recorder: As we are about to move out to join our hearts, hands, and fortunes in the great contest, I think it proper to let the world know something about our regiment's movements. It has scarcely been six weeks since this regiment's organization. It had been recruited up to seven companies, when the first received orders to march. We broke camp at Chelton Hill, near Philadelphia, on Monday morning, April 18th ... arrived in the city about 4 o'clock, and left in an hour afterwards for Baltimore ... on the steamboat Columbia to Annapolis ... attached to the 9th Army Corps, 4th Division, under the command of Gen. Burnside. Signed John C. Brock, Commissary Sergeant, 43d [VERIFY] Reg. U.S.C.T.

articles.headline: Sheba Lodge (juvenile Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria) first anniversary
articles.summary: The First Anniversary of the Sheba Lodge, No. 1, of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria of the juvenile children, came off last Wednesday evening, in the Masonic Hall. The Hall was pretty well filled ... opened with fervent prayer by the Rev. James Hamilton ... a very splendid banner was presented by a gentleman, whose name we cannot just now call to mind. It was painted by Mr. Thomas [VERIFY] Bowser ... Mrs. A. M. Cropper, who was the founder of Sheba Lodge, received the banner, on behalf of the children. articles.headline: Died (Robert H. Purton, Supervisory Committee)
articles.summary: Mr. Robert H. Purton [VERIFY] recently departed this life. He was raised in this city, and, some six or seven years ago, went to England, where men of all kinds have their rights. After the rebellion broke out he saw a chance to help free his brethren. He, therefore, came to the United States and gave himself up to the Supervisory Committee of this city. He was going through a regular drill, and was a very useful man to the Committee.

articles.headline: Eating Saloon (Mrs. Jones, Sixth Street opposite Bethel)
articles.summary: We would call the special attention of our readers to the Eating Saloon of Mrs. Jones, in Sixth Street opposite the Bethel Church. Good accommodations are to be had. Mrs. Jones always has Lunch on hand. Go and help yourselves. She is very polite and accommodating.

articles.headline: Aralena Purnell (concerts at Sansom Street Hall)
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Among the many amusements of the past winter, that have contributed to the pleasure of our citizens, were those inaugurated by this young lady, in the soirees and concerts at Sansom Street Hall, followed by those of the Delmonico, which were received with select and critical audiences. The performances of Aralena Purnell were such as to stamp her as one of the most choice and melodious of singers ... Her sister, Louisa Purnell, (who is quite young,) sang at these concerts. Wishes that Messrs. Clive [?] and Burris [VERIFY], with the choirs of St. Thomas', Bethel, Wesley, the Central Presbyterian, and the Presbyterian Church South Seventh St., would give oratorios; recalls the late Madam Augustus [?] (a sister of Madam Brown).

articles.headline: An Obituary (John Wesley Jefferson, South Camden)
articles.author: H. Davis

articles.summary: Camp near Hanover, Va., June 5, 1864. events.name: A.M.E. General Conference opens at Bethel Church, Philadelphia (first sessions)
events.description: Thirteenth General Conference of the A.M.E. Church convened at Bethel Church, Philadelphia, Monday May 2, 1864, Bishop Quinn presiding; Bishop Nazrey prayed; Bishop Payne read 1 Corinthians 12-13. A. W. Wayman secretary, Eneas McIntosh recording secretary; 138 members. Committee on delegation: J. M. Brown, Beaton Dorrel, W. R. Revels, John Turner, Wm. D. W. Schureman, John Tibbs, George A. Rue, J. Mitchell. Committee on rules (on motion of E. Weaver): E. Weaver, J. P. Campbell, Chas. Burch, Jas. A. Shorter, John A. Warren. Tuesday May 3: M. M. Clark appointed reporter for the Christian Recorder; J. M. Brown and Leonard Patterson for the Daily Advocate and Journal; proceedings to be published in the Daily Press and the Anglo-African. All enrolled delegates seated except A. L. Stanford of the Philadelphia Conference (lacked fifteen days of six years' travel; afterwards admitted), Henry J. Young (Ohio; not admitted), George N. Black (Indiana) and J. M. Wilkerson (Missouri; later admitted). Wednesday May 4 (opened by A. W. Wayman): standing committees named, with Philadelphia Conference members: itinerancy, H. Davis; boundaries, Woodland; slavery and the present condition of the country, J. P. Campbell; Episcopacy, Wm. Moore and W. D. W. Schureman; Book Concern, Standford (sic); missions, S. Smith; education, S. Smith; tracts, J. Woodland; Sabbath schools, S. Smith; revision of discipline, J. P. Campbell and Bro. Schureman; Canadian affairs, Woodland and S. Smith. Thursday May 5 (Bishop Quinn in the chair, opened by F. Tyler?): Wilberforce University petition referred; petition of the church at Wilmington, Del., to be detached from the Baltimore and added to the Philadelphia Conference, carried; a remonstrance against some proceedings of Rev. S. Smith in Philadelphia was read and, after debate (Dr. Watts, J. P. Campbell, W. A. Dove, E. Weaver, N. Peck of Pittsburgh, W. Davis, Bishop Nazrey; S. Smith twice defended himself), referred to the committee on delegation; a petition from Bethel Church, Phila., asking repeal of certain rules referred to revision committee; a second petition from Bethel Church, presented by S. Smith, asking repeal of so much of the discipline as gives the preacher in charge the appointment of the trustees, referred; petition from Riceville, N.J., to leave the Philadelphia for the New York Conference referred to boundaries. Statistics: about 1000 churches, real estate $2,000,000, 40,000 members, 510 travelling and 2000 local preachers. Committee of five on union with the M.E. Church work in the South (M. M. Clark, W. H. Revels, J. M. Brown, A. W. Wayman, J. B. Campbell); special committee of nine on A.M.E./A.M.E. Zion union (H. M. Turner, J. Peck, Wm. D. W. Schureman, J. M. Williams, Wm. A. Dove, E. T. Williams, C. Burch, J. Mitchell). Evening preaching appointments: Tuesday May 3, Bethel, Jacob Mitchell; Bethel at 8, M. F. Sluby; Wesley, Page Tyler; Zion Mission, G. A. Rue; Union, J. P. Shreeves; Burlington, E. E. Davis. Thursday: Bethel, R. H. Cain; Union, S. S. Hammond; Wesley, W. W. Grimes; Camden, J. H. Henson; Burlington, W. H. Hopkins; Zion Mission, D. Rideout.
attendees: General Book Steward and Editor; committee on rules

Philadelphia Conference delegate; committee on Episcopacy

events.name: Remonstrance against Rev. S. Smith and Bethel Church petitions before the General Conference
events.description: A remonstrance against some proceedings of Rev. S. Smith in the city of Philadelphia was presented and read. Dr. Watts said it belonged to the Quarterly Conference; Rev. J. P. Campbell said it contained an implied impeachment of Bro. S. Smith and would, if adopted, deprive him of a seat; Rev. W. A. Dove would refer it back to the protestants; Rev. E. Weaver was for treating it with respect and referring it; Rev. N. Peck of Pittsburgh would send it back; Rev. W. Davis could not see why it came so late; Bishop Nazrey said there was more in the protest than the Conference was aware of. Smith twice defended himself. Referred to the committee on delegation. A petition from Bethel Church, Phila., asked repeal of certain rules of the discipline; a second, presented by S. Smith, asked repeal of the preacher in charge's power to appoint trustees. Both referred to the committee on revision of the discipline. (Context: Stephen Smith had charge of Bethel after J. P. Campbell's resignation in 1863.)

events.name: Daughters of Hope Grand Union Temperance Society, thirteenth convention and installation
events.description: Thirteenth convention of the Daughters of Hope Grand Union (Daughters of Temperance), April 10th [VERIFY; year printed like 1861], with representatives from Philadelphia unions and from Chambersburg, Carlisle and Norristown. Officers installed: Grand P., Sister Bennet [VERIFY]; Grand Associate, Sister Harris [VERIFY]; Grand Treasurer, Sister Fossett [VERIFY]; Grand Conductress, C. Thompson; Grand Sentinel, A. S. Debhart [VERIFY]; Grand Chaplain, Sister Bell. G.P.P. (past officers): Sisters E. Rogers [VERIFY], E. Bowen [VERIFY], M. A. Bundy [VERIFY], E. Newman [VERIFY], E. Davis [VERIFY], Anderson [VERIFY], J. F. Black, E. A. Clark [VERIFY], White, R. Hall [VERIFY].

events.name: A.M.E. General Conference, Bethel Church: sessions of May 6-11 (Episcopal Address, Book Concern, boundaries, S. Smith seated)
events.description: Friday May 6 (Bishop Nazrey presiding): George Thompson, Esq., of England, to address the Conference, collection for Wilberforce University; Rev. J. L. Smith of the (white) Indiana Conference introduced by Willis R. Revels, M.D.; Bishop Payne read the Episcopal Address, 1000 copies ordered printed; Rev. Joseph J. Clinton of the A.M.E. Zion Church introduced; long debate on ordaining men for army chaplaincies (Chaplain Turner, Woodford, W. Dove, J. D. S. Hall, Campbell, W. Davis); the General Book Steward and Editor (E. Weaver) reported for 1860-1864 and presented three volumes of the Christian Recorder; a fund raised for the Book Concern (the ministers paid $142.30 [VERIFY] in cash); committee of three to invite the Hon. George Thompson, M.P.: J. A. Shorter, J. P. Campbell and C. Burch; Weaver chosen to deposit the Book Concern money in a bank until a new Book Steward is elected. Saturday May 7 (Bishop Payne): collection for the Book Concern ($125 [VERIFY]); Henry J. Young's petition debated; Canadian report: both connexions in Canada valid, delegates of the B.M.E. Church seated; committee on union of the A.M.E. and A.M.E. Zion connexions reported (nine elders from each). Monday May 9 (Bishop Quinn): prayer for the Union Army of the Potomac; A. R. Green and party not seated; committee of five on the course of studies: M. M. Clark, J. M. Brown, E. D. Davis, J. P. Campbell, E. Weaver; committee on selecting a site for the Book Concern: S. Smith, W. D. S. [sic] Schureman, E. Weaver; hymn-book revision committee (J. Shorter, J. P. Campbell, Mr. Stanford); Book Steward to publish 2000 hymn books; resolution condemning Major J. Wilkerson as a slanderer; the resolution against the Philadelphia street cars (separate event); boundaries: motion to move Harrisburg from the Baltimore to the Philadelphia Conference LOST; Philadelphia Conference remains as it was; New England merged into New York; a South Carolina Conference to be formed; Chaplain H. M. Turner given leave to return to his regiment. Tuesday May 10 (Bishop Nazrey): death that morning of the eldest daughter of Rev. Geo. W. Johnson reported; temperance report adopted; Mr. Lucas of Vancouver's Island spoke; delay of the church history debated (Campbell, Weaver); petitions from Ebenezer Church and from Bethel Church referred to the discipline committee; marriage resolution signed A. L. Stanford and J. Hamilton; the committee's report in favor of S. Smith holding his seat, 'which had been protested against by some of the members of Bethel Church, Philadelphia,' received and adopted; Solomon A. Thompson to preach at Bethel that night. Wednesday May 11 (Bishop Payne): M.E. Church delegation (Rev. J. Hill, chairman, Drs. Wise and Cunningham) received; Colonel Gregory addressed the Conference; B. Dawson replaced A. T. Hall on the Book Concern committee.

events.name: A.M.E. General Conference condemns exclusion of colored persons from Philadelphia street cars (Streetcar discrimination)
events.description: At the Monday May 9, 1864 session of the A.M.E. General Conference at Bethel Church (Bishop Quinn presiding), a resolution was carried declaring 'that the conduct of the authorities of the street cars of Philadelphia is shameful and disgraceful in the highest degree, in excluding colored persons from the street cars of this city.' Some opposed and others supported it; C. Burch (Rev. Charles Burch, a delegate from outside Philadelphia) spoke in favor. Topic: Streetcar discrimination.

events.name: Lombard Street (colored) Public School concert for the Great Central Sanitary Fair
events.description: Grand musical entertainment by the pupils of the Lombard St. Public School (colored), Fifth Section, under the direction of James M. Bird [VERIFY], assisted by Mr. A. Burris' Concert Troupe, 'in behalf of the Fifth Section, for the benefit of the Sanitary Fair.' Doors 7, performance 8 o'clock; tickets 25 cts. Programme: choruses by the children and the Troupe; solos by Miss H. [?] Carney [VERIFY] ('The Soldier's Friend'), A. Burris ('Let me like a Soldier Die'), Miss Livingston ('Come, come, at your Country's Call'; 'We'll smile and be happy'), Miss Draper ('Long live the moments of pleasure'), Miss K. Carey ('Though a cloud sometimes concealeth'); duet by Miss Carney and A. Burris; 'The Star Spangled Banner' by Miss Livingston and Troupe. Topic: Great Central Fair, Black participation.

events.name: A.M.E. General Conference elects A. W. Wayman and J. P. Campbell bishops; Nazrey dismissed to Canada
events.description: Thursday May 12 (Bishop Quinn): itinerancy report; T. M. D. Ward's California report; motion to exclude A. M. Green (over his comment on the Canada delegation in the Recorder of the 11th) opposed by Rev. E. Weaver and postponed. Friday May 13 (Bishop Nazrey): Episcopacy report adopted; election of bishops fixed for Monday; stewards to furnish a house for the preacher; the Baltimore Conference had left Bishop Nazrey's name out of its minutes. Saturday May 14 ('Philadelphia, May 14'; Bishop Payne): resolution (moved by J. A. Warren) to invite Captain Small, introduced by Bishop Payne, to narrate his daring feats, with a collection for Wilberforce University; committee J. A. Warren, James Lynch and W. D. W. Schureman. Monday May 16: after controversy on expelling Rev. Wm. H. Jones, the Conference went into the election of bishops; tellers Rev. Stephen Smith, John Turner and Leonard Patterson; Rev. A. W. Wayman elected by a large majority, the second balloting elected Rev. J. P. Campbell by a small majority. Tuesday May 17 (Bishop Nazrey): resolution that it was inexpedient for Bishop Nazrey to exercise his functions in the U.S. lost; then carried that he 'be honorably and kindly dismissed to the Canadian service,' with a certificate on parchment drawn by J. Turner, J. M. Brown, J. Warren, J. Tibbs, Schureves [sic], J. M. Williams and Wm. Moore; a General Conference Sabbath School Union formed. Wednesday May 18 (Bishop Payne): 'The constitution of Bethel Church, in Philadelphia, was brought under consideration, in relation to calling a corporation meeting. The preacher in charge has the power to call all such meetings only by the request of any 20 members of the corporation, or the board of trustees'; a large missionary meeting arranged at Bethel Church, committee J. Lynch, R. H. Cain, S. Smith, E. Weaver and A. L. Standford. Thursday May 19 (A. T. Hall opened): 'Philadelphia' struck from the constitution of the Missionary Society and 'Baltimore' inserted; resolution honoring the memory of Bishop Brown [?] and Father Boggs with a collection for their widows.

events.name: Meeting of colored citizens of Philadelphia at Bethel Church addressed by Captain Small of the Planter
events.description: During the General Conference (reported in the minutes of Thursday May 19, 1864): 'At a meeting of colored citizens of Philadelphia, held in Bethel Church, the meeting was addressed by Captain Small, of the Planter. After his brilliant speech, which was listened to with great interest,' Rev. J. M. Warren [sic; J. A. Warren moved the earlier invitation] offered: 'Resolved, That his daring feats, in order to obtain the liberty of his wife, has endeared him to us and to our children forever.' The General Conference had resolved (May 14) that a collection at this meeting go to Wilberforce University. Captain Small is Robert Smalls of the Planter (identification in notes).

events.name: Institute for Colored Youth senior class examination (Greek, Latin, Mathematics)
events.description: Annual private examination of the ICY Senior Class, last week in April 1864, in writing, in Greek, Latin and Mathematics, under the direction of [Pliny?] E. Chase, A.M., of this city (first name blotted on the film). The full question papers are printed (Virgil, Horace, Greek Testament, Homer, Anacreon, geometry, plane and spherical trigonometry). General averages on a scale of ten: Thomas H. Boling 9.67; J. Wesley Cromwell 8.91; Harriet C. Johnson 8.61; Mary V. Brown 8.27; James M. Baxter, jr., 8.21; James L. Smallwood 8.92; Frank J. R. Jones 7.87; Elizabeth Handy 7.67; Margaret A. Masten 7.56; M. Gertrude Offit 7.49; James H. Roberts 7.43 [VERIFY]. Signed E. D. Bassett, Principal.

events.name: A.M.E. General Conference, Bethel Church: sessions of May 20-26 (new bishops preside; J. M. Brown elected editor of the Christian Recorder)
events.description: Editor's note: the Recorder's reporter mislaid the minutes of Saturday and Monday (May 21 and 23). 'Philadelphia, May 20th, 1864' (Bishop Nazrey; S. S. Lewis led services): leave for Bro. Ward to return to California; marriage canon amended so that members divorced for adultery may marry again (Tibbs, J. M. Brown, Burch, Dr. Watts, B. L. Brooks, J. Shorter spoke); petition for lay delegation referred to a special committee: Hall, Schreeves, Tibbs, E. McIntosh, Dove, J. Woodlin, J. Hamilton; members to visit the United States Mint the next day; life membership in the Parent Missionary Society reduced to twenty dollars. Tuesday May 24 (Bishop Nazrey; Brother Williams led services): course of studies adopted; 'Bishop Wayman, the newly elected bishop, took the chair to preside for the first time'; Bishop Campbell made remarks 'quite eloquent in his allusion to his predecessors'; Rev. Elder W. Moore remarked how few of those present had entered the ministry when he did; Father [Burleigh?] said he had been 46 years in the itinerancy and had baptized Bishop Campbell; lay delegation report adopted; report on slavery and the state of the country adopted; Bishop Wayman's paper tendering the thanks of the Conference to President Lincoln referred; Wilberforce treasurer's report received; next General Conference to sit at Washington, D.C.; bishops' salary $300 a year, the Book Steward and travelling preachers the same; certificate for Bishop Nazrey adopted. Thursday May 26 (Bishop Nazrey): on motion of B. S. Brooks, J. M. Brown elected editor of the Christian Recorder (C. Burch's amendment for B. Tanner lost); J. A. Warren elected (General) Book Steward (A. Shorter's substitution not put); a branch Book Depository located at Cincinnati, its book steward the pastor of Allen Chapel; the two offices of Editor and General Book Steward separated; reports on education and on slavery and the condition of the country adopted; Zion Church committee (J. J. Clinton and others) heard on union of the two churches.
attendees: outgoing General Book Steward and Editor

events.name: A.M.E. General Conference (13th) -- ordination of Bishops Wayman and Campbell and Book Concern debates
events.description: Proceedings May 23-26, 1864 at Bethel, Philadelphia. May 23: ordination of Bishops elect Wayman and Campbell by Bishops Quinn, Payne and Nazrey with Elders C. Burch, W. R. Revels and E. Davis; Rev. J. G. Bulah (printed 'Bulengb'; eldest elder) prayed; not less than 2,500 present; collection of $26.44 for the widow Brown and widow Boggs. Rev. T. M. D. Ward named general superintendent of the work in California. Wilberforce University received as common property of the A.M.E. Church; Bishop Payne permitted to go to England on its behalf. May 24: Rev. J. Woodlin opened; Rev. John R. V. Morgan's name erased from the Annual Conference journal on motion of Rev. Wm. Moore. May 25 (Bishop Campbell presiding for the first time): Book Concern to be carried on in the city of Philadelphia; debate on Weaver's substitute report and on separating Editor from General Book Steward (J. M. Brown); motion that E. Weaver be General Book Steward and Editor lost; General Book Steward made amenable to the Philadelphia Annual Conference. Committee of nine on union with the Zion Church: C. Burch, Ind. Conf.; S. Smith, Phila. Conf.; J. A. Warren, Ohio Conf.; J. Turner, Mo. Conf.; J. M. Williams, N. Y. Conf.; J. M. Brown, Balt. Conf.; R. J. Rue (?), N. E. Conf.; E. Weaver, Phila. Conf.; J. Hall (?), Balt. Conf. Reserve committee J. Woodlin and A. L. Stanford. May 26: Rev. S. M. Giles (Zion) spoke on union; vote of thanks to the Pennsylvania Railroad Company for tickets to Pittsburg; Bro. Turner placed in Bishop Campbell's stead on the hymn-book; B. T. Tanner moved as General Editor (laid on table); Bishop Payne took leave. The paper's own 'General Conference' paragraph (p. 2, col. 7) says it closed on the 26th ultimo, the longest General Conference yet held.

events.name: Wilberforce University -- Philadelphia District treasurer's annual report
events.description: Treasurer Maurice Hall reports $503.51 paid over. Bethel collections and gifts totalling $329.82: three special collections of Bethel Church $82.82; Rev. Stephen Smith $50; teachers and scholars of Bethel Sunday school $60; the Ladies' Fair $100; Henry Gordon $5; Sarah Gordon $5; Rev. James Frisby $5; Rev. J. P. Campbell $5 (or 6); Lewis R. Seymour $10; Maurice Hall $5; Miss Maria Wallere (?) $5; Miss Mary Still $2; Miss Ann Laws $2; Miss Wilson $5. From the District, $173.69: Revs. William Moore $30, Henry Davis $25, William Offer $15, J. Gould $20.65 (?), J. L. Standford $7, W. D. W. Schureman $15, Elisha Weaver $10, James Hollen $8.48, by Rev. Elisha Weaver from a Friend $6, Richard Barney $11.80, Abram Cripple (?) $8, Peter Gardiner $7, by Rev. Elisha Weaver from a Friend $1.60, Jeremiah Young $7.66. He adds that Bethel Church has paid $329.82 and 'has not been slack on the subject'.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference, 48th session
events.location: Mount Pisgah Church, Salem, N. J.
events.description: Sessions May 30 - June 2, 1864. Bishop Nazrey presiding, assisted by Bishop Quinn (June 1 'Bishop William Paul Quinn'). Secretary Rev. J. Woodlin (on motion of Rev. J. H. Smith); assistant Rev. W. D. W. Schureman. Finance: Revs. Hollen, Stanford and J. H. Smith. Rev. William Moore treasurer of the Widows' Fund. Two-cent money reported: Rev. J. Hollen $2.48; Till $3.30; J. H. Smith $2; R. Barney $4; J. H. Henson $4; William Moore $5; J. Young $4.63; A. L. Stanford $9; Theodore Gould $10; A. C. Crispin (?) $11.15; W. R. Norris $8.53 (?); W. W. Winder $1.30; J. Cornish $2.50; Edward Lewis (?) $5.40; J. W. Stephens $1; W. Offer $7; J. Jay $1.75; J. Long $2; P. Gardiner $?.25; H. Davis $1; T. Cuff $3. May 31: complaint of Rev. H. Davis against Shadrach Blackson (printed 'Shadrac Blackson') for non-attendance laid on table. Committees: Orders and Receptions, Revs. W. D. W. Schureman, A. L. Stanford, P. Gardiner; Letters and Memorials, Schureman, T. Grot (?), R. Barney (printed 'Berney'); Sabbath-schools, T. H. Cooper, H. Davis, J. Young; Missions, J. Woodlin, T. W. Henry, James Hollen; Temperance, Jos. Smith, J. H. Henson, A. Till; State of the Country, Schureman, Hollen, Stanford; Publication of Minutes, E. Weaver, J. Woodlin, A. L. Stanford. Deacon's orders (if examination sustained): W. Offer, E. Laws, J. H. Long, J. P. Jay, T. Cuff, J. W. Stevenson, Redmond Fawcett. Elder's orders: J. C. Cornish and W. H. Wynder. June 1: Bishop J. P. Campbell addressed Conference; committee (A. L. Stanford, Rev. J. Woodlin, T. Good [Gould?]) to draw up an address to Bishop Nazrey and present him a suit of clothes; $52.65 (?) presented. Rev. Mr. Hardy, local preacher from the 'Israel Church', received; Rev. Mr. Isaiah Brodie (printed 'Brodlio'), from the M. E. Church, received. June 2: Bishop Quinn called on Rev. Elisha Weaver to open; Bishop ruled no member could be expelled for neglect of duty without trial; Rev. H. J. Rhodes (Baltimore District, appointed to Wilmington, Del.) chose to remain in the Baltimore Conference, Delaware having been transferred to the Philadelphia District by the General Conference; Rev. Isaac J. Pindle (?) the same.
attendees: Rev.; committee on Orders and Receptions

events.name: Philadelphia Mission Sabbath School -- preaching resumed
events.location: Hall, south-east corner of Broad and Lombard Streets, Philadelphia
events.description: Preaching resumed under the superintendency of Rev. James Frisby of Bethel A.M.E. Church on behalf of the Philadelphia City Mission; Sabbath school at 9 A.M. and 1 P.M. Signed Rev. James Frisby (signature printed indistinctly).
attendees: Rev.; superintendent, of Bethel A.M.E. Church

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church (Coates St.) -- change of pastors: valedictories of Nazrey and Schureman, inaugural of A. L. Stanford
events.location: Union A.M.E. Church, Coates Street, Philadelphia; Bethany Mission, corner of 19th (?) and Spring Garden Sts.
events.description: Sunday June 12, 1864, 8 P.M.: Bishop W. Nazrey's valedictory address at Union A.M.E., Coates St.; same day 3 P.M.: Rev. A. L. Stanford's inaugural biennial discourse there. Sunday June 19, 8 P.M.: Rev. W. D. W. Schureman's valedictory at Union; 10 1/2 A.M. the same day: Stanford's inaugural at the Bethany Mission, corner of 19th (?) and Spring Garden Sts. Implies Stanford's 1864 appointment to Union (with Bethany Mission).

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference -- election of Book Concern trustees and closing business
events.description: Continuation of the 48th Philadelphia Annual Conference. Thursday June 2: reports of committees on letters and petitions and on itinerancy; Brother Steward received; case of the Macedonia Church as connected with the Canesville (?) Sabbath School. Friday (printed 'June 4th', evidently June 3): Bishop Nazrey presiding, Brother Till prayed; Fuller (printed 'Fulley'/'Foller') placed back into the Frankford Church with his certificate; case of J. B. Parker referred to a committee of three. Book Concern trustees elected per charter: E. Weaver, chairman; J. Woodlin; Theodore Gould; Joseph H. Smith; Redman Faucett; Stephen Smith; Wm. Moore. Saturday June 4 (printed 'June 5th'): reports on Sabbath schools and ordination; J. H. Haslett (?) recommended for Conference membership, also Brother Norris; ordination as deacons recommended for Bros. Stevenson, Offer, Long, Laws, Cuff, Fausett and Jay.

events.name: Book Concern trustees meeting -- Weaver made General Editor; Stephen Smith treasurer
events.description: Board of Trustees of the A.M.E. Book Concern: Rev. Elisha Weaver chairman; present Revs. Elisha Weaver, William Moore, Joseph Smith, Theo. Gould, Stephen Smith and Redmon Fausett (secretary). Committee of Elders Moore, S. Smith and the General Book Steward to select a suitable place for the Book Concern. Bishop Wayman, present, suggested the General Book Steward be General Editor: resolved that Rev. Elisha Weaver become General Editor of the Christian Recorder. Rev. S. Smith elected Treasurer; moneys over $50 to be paid to him; monthly reports. District corresponding editors: Baltimore, Rev. Benjamin T. Tanner; Philadelphia, Rev. A. L. Stanford; New York, Rev. Leonard Patterson; New England, Rev. W. W. Grimes; Ohio, Dr. Samuel Watts; Indiana, Rev. Aeneas McIntosh; Missouri, Rev. M. M. Clark; California, Rev. T. M. D. Ward.

events.name: Frederick Douglass Lyceum -- semi-annual election
events.description: Officers elected for six months: President Wm. C. Banton; Vice President Horace F. Owens; Secretary John H. Davis; Treasurer J. Wesley Cromwell; Librarian T. J. Minton; Critic Joseph H. Rodgers; Executive Committee Horace T. [sic] Owens, Francis M. Seymour, James M. Baxter. Notice signed John H. Davis, Secretary, Philadelphia, June 14th, 1864.

events.name: A.M.E. / A.M.E. Zion union convention
events.description: Met June 14 (no quorum), reassembled June 15. Supt. J. D. Brooks (Zion) president pro tem.; Rev. William Moore prayed. Committee of five (Rev. Wm. D. W. Schureman, chairman) reported: President, Bishop A. W. Wayman; Vice-Presidents, Supt. Clinton, Supt. William Bishop, Bishop J. P. Campbell, Revs. Giles, Cain and A. L. Stanford. Brother Cain read the A.M.E. preamble and propositions; Zion report read by Rev. S. T. Jones; parts of each preamble adopted; A.M.E. first proposition adopted; debate on the episcopacy (Zion substitute: superintendents elected for life without imposition of hands). The editor (p. 2, col. 1) reports it adjourned 'last Thursday night', having ratified the delegates' work; editor of the Anglo-African (Mr. Hamilton) attended.

events.name: A.M.E. Zion General Conference in Philadelphia (with joint union committee at Bethel, May 27)
events.description: Zion General Conference sessions May 25 - June 14, 1864, at Wesley Church, Lombard St. Superintendents W. H. Bishop and J. J. Clinton presiding. A.M.E. committee (Revs. A. McIntosh, M. F. Sluby, Dr. S. Watts) proposed union; Zion joint committee met the A.M.E. committee in Bethel Church, May 27, 6 P.M. (J. D. Brooks chairman; J. M. Brown and J. P. Hamer secretaries; benediction by Rev. J. Woodlin); convention called for Wesley Church June 14. Zion delegates to the convention for the Philadelphia Conference: S. Talbot, S. T. Jones, J. B. Trusty, C. J. Carter; reserve J. H. Anderson. Death of Rev. Dr. Samuel Tiffany Gray (pastor, Wesley Zion, Washington) reported June 1; his body brought to Philadelphia and funeral held June 4 at Wesley Church, Lombard St., sermon by Elder B. G. Bolden (?). Superintendents elected: J. J. Clinton, S. Talbot, J. D. Brooks, J. W. Loguen (later declined), then W. H. Bishop (June 13). Illness (June 7) and death (announced June 14) of Elder Prince G. Laws 'in this city'. Elder W. T. Biddle (?) ill in the city. Remarks on slavery by George T. Downing of New York. A.M.E. ministers visited June 8.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference -- 1864 appointments
events.description: Stations: Bethel church, Pa., Wm. Moore; Union Bethel, Pa., A. L. Stanford; Wesley, Pa., J. H. Smith; Mission, Pa., W. W. Winder; Trenton, N. J., Thomas Cooper, subject to H. Davis; Camden, N. J., Theophelus Stewart, subject to W. Moore; New Brunswick, N. J., William Offer, subject to [blank]. Circuits: Thorntown (?), Pa., J. Cornish, subject to E. Weaver; West Chester, Pa., E. Lawe [Laws], subject to E. Weaver; Frankford, Pa., A. C. Cripen; Danville (?), Pa., J. H. Henson; Reading, Pa., W. R. Norris, subject to J. H. Henson; Burlington, N. J., Theodore Gould; Pennington-ville, Pa., James B. Pierse, subject to J. Browden (?); Oxford, Pa., Isaiah Brown, subject to [blank]; Freehold, Pa. [sic], J. W. Stevenson, subject to J. Hollen; Princeton, N. J., Henry Davis; Bordentown, N. J., James Hollen; Snow Hill, N. J., T. W. Henry; West Philadelphia, P. Gardener; Woodbury, N. J., Richard Barnes; Bridgeton, N. J., J. Woodlin; Cape May, N. J., Jacob James, subject to J. Woodlin; Salem, N. J., Joseph H. Long, subject to [blank]; Wilmington, Del., H. J. Rhodes; Lewistown, Pa., to be supplied; Laurel, Del., to be supplied; Smyrna, Del., G. Waters; Camden, Del., W. H. Williams; Frederick, Del., [blank], subject to Andrew Till. Followed by Princeton circuit quarterly meetings (Princeton July 9-10, Brunswick July 16-17, Rocky Hill July 23-24, Mounten [?] July 30-31), Rev. H. Davis, Elder of Princeton Circuit.

events.name: Dedication of the A.M.E. Church, Mount Holly, N. J.
events.description: Dedication announced for Sunday June 26, 1864, 10 A.M. and afternoon; Bishops Quinn, Wayman and Campbell expected; aim to raise $300. Notice signed T. Gould, minister in charge (Theodore Gould was appointed to Burlington circuit).

events.name: District Grand Lodge No. 2, Independent Order of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria -- annual meeting and installation
events.location: New Masonic Hall, South 11th St., Philadelphia
events.description: Officers for the year: R. H. Gleaves, R.W.G. Chief; Sister Anna M. Cropper, R.W.G.P. Daughter; Thos. Jones, R.W.G.V. Chief; Sister E. Miller, R.W.G.D. of Fount; J. [Jonathan] Davis, M.D., R.W.G.R. Secretary; Sister Sarah Jenkins, R.W.G.D. of Records; Henry Carter, R.W.G.F. Secretary; Sister A. Hollingsworth, R.W.G.F. Daughter; Stephen Smith, R.W.G. Treasurer; Sister E. B. Randolph, R.W.G.D. Treasurer; James Hamilton, R.W.G. Prelate; Sister H. Wilson, R.W.G.D. of Lesson; N. L. Durham, R.W.G. Orator; Wm. A. H. Smith, W.G. Conductor; Sister Esther Ambrowe [Ambrose?], W.G.D. Conductor; Jas. Dolphin (printed 'Doiphio'), W.G.I. Sent.; Sister Julia Jackson, W.G.D. of K.; Jas. C. Goldsboro (printed 'Goldshoro'), W.G.O. Sent.; Sister Mary Balie, W.G.D. of P.; Henry Thomas, R.W.D.G. Chief; Sister Jane Moore, R.W.P.G.P. Daughter. Signed R. H. Gleaves, R.W.G. Chief; attest Jonathan Davis, M.D., R.W.G.R. Sec. The order's initials are printed 'I. O. of G. S. and D. of S.' (Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria).

events.name: Fraternal Association -- anniversary dinner
events.description: Anniversary dinner of the Fraternal Association, 5:30 P.M., 'last Wednesday evening, the 21st inst.' (Wednesday was June 22, 1864). Guests included 'the noble and brave Captain Small', Mr. Crummel the printer, Rev. Mr. Mains (?) (president of the Society), Mr. O. V. Catto and the editor (Weaver). Bill of fare printed; toasts to the day, sister societies, guests, the press and woman.

notes: CR_1864-04-02: Death of Mrs. Mary C. Weaver, wife of editor Rev. Elisha Weaver, is the issue's main Philadelphia item: two memorial poems (p1, 'Mrs. M. C. Weaver', Norfolk and Providence), H. M. Turner's condolence (p2), J. H. Turpin's eulogy (p2, calls her 'my dear mother'), and a Washington letter (p1) all mourn her. No death date in this issue; the death was evidently reported in a March issue (cr64q1). Probably the Mrs. Mary C. Weaver of the 1862 'Good News' cutting-system ad; identification in notes only.

CR_1864-04-02: James Wiggins, mourned by the Bethel Sabbath School Teachers' Association (Mar 21) and the Bethel Sacred Musical Association (Mar 23), is probably the Recorder's city carrier James Wiggins (recurring 1861 carrier notice); the resolutions call him 'a young man of much future promise'. Identification not stated in the paper.
CR_1864-04-02: Esther Armstrong (Wiggins committees) is probably the Esther Armstrong of the 1863 Soldiers' Relief Association notice; identification in notes only.
CR_1864-04-02: 'Mr. W. S. Walker' of Frankford is probably Wm. S. Walker, barber, 22 Main St., Frankford (1863 ad).
CR_1864-04-02: John Oliver's Intelligence Office now gives Pine Street between 11th and 12th (previously Clarkson Hall, 615 Cherry), so entered as a changed ad.

CR_1864-04-02: J. C. Bustil, ACS trustee of Philadelphia, is possibly Joseph C. Bustill; not linked as identified. Benj. Coates (white Quaker colonizationist) is mentioned in text only. R. H. Cain is of Brooklyn here.

CR_1864-04-09: Elder J. P. Campbell assisting at the Port Republic, N.J. dedication is presumably J. P. Campbell; not linked from this letter since only author/out-of-scope; Port Republic is in the NJ field of the Philadelphia Conference. Signature read 'Harriet A. Smith' (blurred).

CR_1864-04-16: 'Rev. Peter Gardiner' of Princeton, N.J. (printed Gardioer/Gardiner) is presumably the elder of the Bordentown Circuit notice (Apr 2); Gardiner/Gardener and Dr. P. Gardiner remain under review per owner, so no identification.
CR_1864-04-16: Caroline Johnson (printed Johnston and Johnson) is the well-known Philadelphia wax-fruit maker; identification in notes only.

White officers (Fribley, Burritt, Bailey, Heichhold, Tilghman, Heimach) are not linked.
